cloudSync.title: Cloud Sync
cloudSync.connectHint: Sync manual hosts and snippets across devices through an encrypted private Gist.
cloudSync.autoSyncHint: Sync when hosts or snippets change, and when the window becomes visible again.
cloudSync.syncPasswordsHint: Uploads saved login passwords with the payload. They are protected by the sync password's encryption, but stored on GitHub's servers in encrypted form. Off by default.
cloudSync.setPasswordHint: Encrypts the cloud vault. The password never leaves this device — losing it means the cloud data cannot be decrypted.
cloudSync.passwordTooShort: The sync password needs at least 8 characters.
cloudSync.passwordMismatch: The two passwords do not match.
cloudSync.unlockHint: Enter the sync password to decrypt the cloud vault.
cloudSync.lockHint: Change the password (the next sync re-uploads under the new one) or lock it again.
cloudSync.historyHint: Restoring pushes the old data back as a new version; other devices pick it up automatically.
cloudSync.conflictHint: The cloud vault was encrypted with a different sync password. Enter that password to adopt the cloud data, or push this device's data instead.
cloudSync.mergeConflictNote: Both sides edited {count} item(s); the local version was kept. Check the version history if something is missing.
cloudSync.blockedHint: The upload would drop far more data than usual — this looks like a local failure, not a deliberate cleanup. Nothing was written to the cloud.
cloudSync.emptyHint: This device has no hosts or snippets, but the cloud vault has data. Restoring pulls the cloud data down; pushing replaces it with this device's (empty) state.
cloudSync.gistLinked: Connected — syncs into your private Gist
cloudSync.gistMissing: Connected — no sync Gist yet (created on first sync)
cloudSync.stepOpen: 1. Click the button below to open the GitHub activation page and enter the device code:
cloudSync.stepWait: 2. After authorizing, this page completes the connection on its own — please wait…

keySetup.donePasswordOff: Key login is set up and password login is off
keySetup.doneBackup: The server's SSH settings were changed; a backup is kept at
keySetup.donePasswordRemoved: The password saved in OmnySSH was removed.
keySetup.donePasswordOn: Key login works. Password login is still on — OmnySSH needs sudo without a password prompt to change server settings.
keySetup.failedMayBeOff: Key setup failed — password login may be off
keySetup.failedMayBeOffHint: The server's SSH settings may have been changed. Password login may be off now, or after the SSH service next restarts. The new key was saved for this host.
keySetup.failedCheckHint: To see, open a terminal and run
keySetup.failedRestoreHint: To turn passwords back on, restore
keySetup.failedRestoreHintEnd: and reload sshd. If you can't log in, use your hosting provider's console.
keySetup.rolledBack: Password login was turned back on
keySetup.rolledBackHint: A step after password login was turned off failed, so OmnySSH restored the server's SSH settings from its backup. Password login works as before.
keySetup.confirmStepReuse: Reuse the login key OmnySSH made before, or create it again if it is gone:
keySetup.confirmStepCreate: Create a login key on this computer:
keySetup.confirmStepAddMid: so this computer logs in without a password
keySetup.confirmStepDisable: Turn off password login on the server for every account and device, if your account can use sudo without a password. A backup of the server's SSH settings is kept.
keySetup.confirmNote: Password login is turned off only after the new key is tested. Keep the key file: if you lose it, you'll need your hosting provider's console to get back in.
